 Insecurity Insight – Monitoring incidents around the world affecting aid, health care, education, and protection. 
 
Data collected by Insecurity Insight shows that between 07 October 2023 and 23 June 2026, at least 3,354 incidents of violence against or obstruction of access to health care took place across the occupied Palestinian territory.
 1
 95% of all incidents were attributed to Israeli forces. 
● Gaza: 2,339 attacks on health care were recorded during which health facilities were damaged 448 times, 770 health workers were killed and 398 arrested.
 2
 Patient access to medicine was obstructed on 303 occasions. ● West Bank and East Jerusalem: 947 attacks on health care were recorded during which health facilities were damaged 30 times, 12 health workers were killed and 190 arrested. Patient access to medicine was obstructed on 585 occasions. 
View the incidents on our interactive map. Download the data. Updated every Monday and includes information on weapons use, perpetrators and effects. For data enquiries, please get in touch. Data is continuously updated and numbers may change if/ when further information is made available. See here for methodology.

Other resources Insecurity Insight has released a report examining how the conflict between Iran, Israel, Lebanon and the US has impacted emergency medical services across the Greater Middle East region. 
Key findings ● The highest number of incidents affecting emergency medical services were recorded in Lebanon ● Nearly three quarters of incidents were attributed to Israeli forces ● Sequential strikes on emergency responders were documented in Iran, Iraq and Lebanon. ● Emergency responders in southern Lebanon reported delays and heightened risks during rescue operations.

This document comprises threats and violence as well as protests and other events affecting the delivery of and access to health care. It is part of the Attacks on Health Care project by Insecurity Insight. It is prepared from information available in local, national and international news outlets and online databases. The incidents reported are not a complete nor a representative list of all events that affected the provision of health care and have not been independently verified through ground investigations. Article 6 A Member of the United Nations which has persistently violated the Principles contained in the present Charter may be expelled from the Organization by the General Assembly upon the recommendation of the Security Council.

Accordingly, our respective Governments, through representatives assembled in the city of San Francisco, who have exhibited their full powers found to be in good and due form, have agreed to the present Charter of the United Nations and do hereby establish an international organization to be known as the United Nations.
